hook: Lion NTCP cannot bind hepatitis B virus, while cat, tiger and leopard versions can
hook_turn: while cat, tiger and leopard versions can
summary: NTCP is the liver transporter that hepatitis B virus uses to enter cells. Comparing versions from 23 mammals, the team found two amino acid changes (positions 191 and 268) that make lion NTCP lose virus binding and much of its bile acid transport. Swapping them between cat and lion NTCP flipped the effect. Most data come from cultured cells and simulation, with infection shown in cat liver cells.
title: Hepadnavirus tropism determined by diversified NTCP functionality in Feline species
